## Recommended first contact: American University Washington College of Law

Start with **AUWCL**, *if public-interest/public-service work is a genuine fit*. It has the strongest potential funding upside: its PIPS program is a **three-year, full-tuition** scholarship. The official search result describes it as financial and programmatic support for entering full-time J.D. students with strong credentials and demonstrated desire/potential for public-interest or public-service work. That potential award is substantial enough to make it the first priority, even though Maryland Carey Law currently has the easiest immediately usable admissions-outreach option.

### 1) AUWCL — funding-first next move
- **What PIPS is for (plain English):** It supports incoming full-time J.D. students who have both strong academic credentials and a credible commitment to public-interest/public-service legal work.
- **What to do:** Complete both the general J.D. application and the separate **electronic PIPS Scholarship Application**. The official PIPS application-and-selection result says they must be submitted electronically, with PIPS essays, résumé, and a recommendation letter. Its stated deadline is **January 31, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. EST**.
- **Application information link:** [PIPS Application and Selection Process (official AU result)](https://www.google.com/search?q=site%3Aamerican.edu%2Fwcl%2Fimpact+%22PIPS+Application+and+Selection+Process%22). This is the official page identified by AU in the results; it is where AU provides the electronic-application instructions.
- **Open tab:** I left AUWCL’s official **Office of Public Interest** page open (tab 21), with its “Public Interest/Service Scholarship” navigation item visible. I attempted to open that dedicated item directly, but its link currently points to the older `www.wcl.american.edu` host, which triggered a certificate/privacy error in the browser. I therefore did not represent that failed page as readable proof.

### 2) Maryland Carey Law — easiest immediate admissions outreach
- **Request materials:** On Carey’s **Contact Admissions** page, use **“Request Information: JD Applicants.”** The same page supplies a direct fallback: **admissions@law.umaryland.edu**, **(410) 706-3492**, Monday–Friday **9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.**
- **Realistic online event:** **JD Admissions 101 Webinar — Thursday, August 13, 2026, 12:00–1:00 p.m.** The school’s JD Webinar schedule provides a “Register here” link for it. (Other listed online options include a September 3 JD Admissions 101 webinar, 5:00–6:00 p.m.)
- **Next move:** Submit the JD-information request, then register for the August 13 webinar and ask how public-interest applicants can best position scholarship applications.
- **Open tab:** I left Carey’s official **JD Webinars** details/schedule page open in **tab 7**.

### 3) University of Baltimore School of Law — clearest one-to-one admissions route
- **How to schedule:** Use the official **30-minute phone-call registration form**: [Speak with UBalt Law | Fall 2026](https://forms.lsac-unite.org/5810/UBaltLawPhoneCallFall2026.html). It is explicitly for a scheduled call with an Admissions Office member and asks you to select a session.
- **Available format/times:** The form lists Eastern Time slots beginning at **11:00–11:30 a.m.** and **11:30 a.m.–12:00 p.m.**, with dates from **September 30 through December 3, 2026**.
- **Backup contact:** **lawadmissions@ubalt.edu** or **410-837-4459** (business hours listed as 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.).
- **Alternative event:** The visit page lists a **Fall Virtual Open House, Tuesday, October 27, 2026, 6:00–7:00 p.m. ET via Zoom**, no registration required, password **UBaltLaw**.
- **Next move:** Choose one phone slot and bring three targeted questions: part-time/evening fit, scholarship/aid review timing, and public-interest experiential opportunities.
- **Open tab:** I left the actual UBalt **phone-call registration form** open in **tab 10**.

## Simple outreach order
1. **AUWCL:** confirm PIPS eligibility/materials immediately and begin the separate scholarship package.
2. **Maryland Carey:** request JD materials and register for the August 13 online admissions session.
3. **UBalt:** book a 30-minute admissions call using the open form.

This order prioritizes the unusually consequential PIPS funding opportunity while still taking advantage of Carey’s low-friction information request and UBalt’s straightforward individual appointment system.

Then go to the University of Baltimore School of Law site and find the instructions for scheduling an admissions meeting by opening the relevant admissions event or meeting page and pulling the registration link or contact method from the actual details page, and keep that page open too so I can compare the two schools side by side. After that, on American University Washington College of Law’s site, find the PIPS Scholarship page and give me a short plain-English summary of what the scholarship is for, along with the application form link, because funding could change which school I prioritize; if there’s a dedicated scholarship page, leave that open in another tab as proof. Once you’ve gathered all of that, recommend which of these three schools I should contact first based on the best mix of easy admissions outreach and potential funding, and include the specific action or contact details you found for each school so I have a simple next move.
